claims: Driving Under the Influence (DUI) in Virginia involves operating a vehicle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of 0.08% or higher.
Driving Under the Influence (DUI) in Virginia involves operating a vehicle under the influence of drugs.
First-time DUI offenses in Virginia are Class 1 misdemeanors.
First-time DUI offenses in Virginia are punishable by up to 12 months in jail.
First-time DUI offenses in Virginia are punishable by $250–$2,500 in fines.
First-time DUI offenses in Virginia are punishable by a 12-month license suspension.
A BAC of 0.15%–0.20% brings mandatory minimum jail time of 5-10 days.
Second DUI offenses within 5 years require 20 days mandatory jail time.
Third DUI offenses are Class 6 felonies.
DUI convictions require mandatory Alcohol Safety Action Program (ASAP) enrollment.
DUI convictions require ignition interlock device installation.
A DUI conviction in Virginia creates a permanent criminal record.
A DUI conviction's criminal record cannot be expunged in Virginia.
Driving under the influence of drugs (including prescription medication) is illegal with the same penalties as alcohol-related DUI.
A DUID conviction adds 6 demerit points to the driving record.
Drivers under 21 with a BAC of 0.02% to less than 0.08% can be convicted of illegal consumption of alcohol.
